crossRefs.note: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
“If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.
Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom. God may refute him, not man;’
I was mute with silence. I held my peace, even from good. My sorrow was stirred.
My heart was hot within me. While I meditated, the fire burned. I spoke with my tongue:
If I say, I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning…
For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
As for me, I said in my haste, “I am cut off from before your eyes.” Nevertheless you heard the voice of my petitions…
I said in my haste, “All people are liars.”
He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
She came in immediately with haste to the king, and asked, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the…
So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

translations.web: “Therefore my thoughts answer me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
translations.bsb: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
translations.kjv: Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for this I make haste.
translations.asv: Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, Even by reason of my haste that is in me.
